source.title: Which Relations Can Be Generalized Implicitly?

record.file_problem: The post text is present, but mathematical notation and plot contents are partly lost or omitted; exact plotted values cannot be read.
record.tranche_reason: It tests implicit generalization on group-operation and set-matching tasks, rather than reproducing the original modular-addition setup.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative outcomes for group-operation tasks and set matching. It refers to plots without providing their values in the text. Background claims attributed to cited work are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The post trains small networks on new algorithmic group, monoid and set-matching tasks and describes whether and how fast they 'grok'. This bears on V1 in new settings. However, the text gives only qualitative outcomes: no training-accuracy saturation, no delay length and no accuracy values. The plots are not in the text, so no row can show V1's delayed jump.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the author explicitly flags the whole group section as possibly wrong because of a methodological flaw, while saying the set-matching results stand. The author conjectures that transformers implicitly generalize problems solvable in constant time by a small rule set with an algebraic oracle.
record.recipe_differences: The post studies group-operation generalization and synthetic set matching, rather than modular arithmetic grokking; it does not report the original training-dynamics measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported result for truncated infinite groups changes after using a comparable setup that avoids the reduced training-data-per-element problem.

fits_no_version.finding: Abelian groups are described as grokking faster than non-abelian groups; monoids vary. The group section is partly retracted by the author.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The speed of grokking group operations depends on algebraic structure (abelian faster than non-abelian).

fits_no_version.finding: A set-membership linear probe dips just before generalization on the set-matching task and then recovers. In toy models it rises, indicating a linear set representation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A linear representation of latent set membership accompanies implicit generalization of transitive matching relations.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out edge generalization on set matching appears only with enough training edges (none at 6, some at 12, proper at 24).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Implicit generalization of set-matching relations requires a minimum number of training relations.

record.problems: The group results are qualitative and do not include accuracy or training-dynamics values. The post explicitly acknowledges a serious flaw in the initial group methodology. The plots are not available in the supplied text, and there are no reported uncertainty estimates or null controls.
record.rows_left_out: The post mentions 18 training edges but does not state an outcome in the text, and the plotted result is unavailable; no row was recorded. Probe trends described only across an unspecified range of edge counts are represented as aggregate trends rather than assigned to individual counts.

untested.parts: Training-accuracy saturation, a chance-level test period followed by a jump to near-perfect accuracy, and delay growing as the training set shrinks are not reported numerically in the text.

missing.what: Plotted training/test accuracy curves for the 12 group/monoid tasks and the set-matching runs (including 18 edges). These would be needed to judge V1's delay, but they are absent from the text.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal LessWrong post with no numbers in the text. The group results are partly retracted. It is not an original source. No verdict labels are given because every V1-linked row is cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not report training-accuracy saturation, a chance-level test-accuracy period, a later jump to near-perfect accuracy, or a comparison showing that smaller training sets require more optimization.
The set-membership probe is not a test of the stated Fourier/generalizing-circuit mechanism or of later removal of memorizing components.
No image, text, or molecule training regime is tested, nor are initialization scale or weight norm varied.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
The study does not test weight decay, low-norm circuit efficiency, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
It does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs or architectures.
Optimizer instabilities and floating-point or softmax artifacts are not controlled or tested.

rows.subject: Not stated
rows.operation_detail: Train on group-operation examples and assess generalization

conditions.value: Three abelian groups: cyclic and products of cyclic groups

rows.value: The abelian groups grok pretty quickly.
rows.note: Reported as an aggregate over three groups; the text does not give per-group results or training-time and accuracy values.
rows.check: 'Grok pretty quickly' gives no train/test curves or delay. The author's EDIT says the group section had a serious methodological flaw, so the result is of doubtful reliability. Subject architecture is not stated.

rows.subject: Not stated
rows.operation_detail: Train on group-operation examples and assess generalization
rows.note: Reported as an aggregate over three groups; no timing, training accuracy, or test accuracy values are supplied.
rows.check: 'Grok slowly' suggests a longer delay for non-abelian groups but gives no values. The same EDIT flaw caveat applies.

rows.subject: Not stated
rows.operation_detail: Train on truncated infinite-group operation examples and assess generalization
rows.value: They do not seem to grok at all in the initial setup.
rows.note: The author later says the initial result was a training-data artifact: truncation reduced the amount of training data per element.
rows.check: The 'don't grok' result was retracted by the author as a training-data artifact (less training data per element). It should be treated as superseded, not as absence of grokking.

rows.note: The post gives no accuracy or training-dynamics values.
rows.check: Only says the network 'learned' the free group. No timing relative to training-accuracy saturation is given, so V1's delay cannot be judged.
